lead: A conversation between people as a column of messages: who wrote each one, what kind it is (the customer's, the agent's, an internal note), when, the text with its mentions in bold, and the files. `MessageComposer` is the box under it, with a switch between the ways of writing (reply, internal note). For a conversation with an AI assistant see [Chat Thread](/chat-thread).

messages.customer: Hi, how do I invite a teammate to our workspace, and give them read-only access?
messages.note: @Ada Lin can you look at this one? The customer has asked twice.
messages.agent: Hi Priya, go to Settings → Team → Invite, and pick the Viewer role. I have sent you the steps too.

modes.notePlaceholder: Write a note for the team, @ mentions someone…

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: `messages` are the data and `kinds` say how each kind looks: a label and the `variant` / `color` of the [Callout](/callout) it sits in. `mentions` are the names that can be mentioned. A text keeps its line breaks; a message with a node as its body shows it as it is.

relative.title: Relative time
relative.description: `relativeTime` says "1 hour ago" instead of the date; the date is the tooltip.

composer.title: Composer
composer.description: `modes` are the ways of writing; the switch shows with two or more. A mode with `mentions` has a box that takes `@`. `toolbar` is what you add above the box (a function gets the mode), and `onSend` gets the text and the mode. The draft is yours: keep one per mode when each should remember its own.
composer.suggestion: Hi Priya, you can invite a teammate under Settings → Team → Invite.

conversation.title: A conversation
conversation.description: Both together: write a reply or a note and it joins the thread.

styling.title: Styling Reference
styling.description: MessageThread and MessageComposer have no slot of their own: a message is a Callout, with an Avatar, Text, Tag and Link; the composer is a Segmented, a Textarea or Mentions, and a Button.
